zweck.akte.Reich: What you build and maintain: major projects, wonders, heritage and armed forces.

zweck.tab.schreibtisch: Daily business: what is due today, what the game warns about and what your staff advises.
zweck.tab.zeitung: The country in headlines: the same reality in different framings, and the poll of the month.
zweck.tab.gespraech: Free language: you ask, the game explains and proposes steps for you to confirm.
zweck.tab.personen: Who governs with you: cabinet, partners, promises and their deadlines.
zweck.tab.chronik: The memory of your term: decisions, events and polls.
zweck.tab.speicher: Your saved game: save, store in slots, export as a file or restore from a file.
zweck.tab.politik: Policy by area: pick an area to see the situation, acute problems and every measure you can take there.
zweck.tab.bereiche: What has the biggest lever today: projects the game derives from your acute problems.
zweck.tab.programme: Government programmes: goals over several steps, and every step demands real policy.
zweck.tab.beschluesse: What has been decided and is being implemented: schedule, costs and record of decisions.
zweck.tab.wirkungsbericht: What your decisions achieved: six and twelve months later, with trend, regions and side effects.
zweck.tab.netz: The whole web of effects: every quantity, every problem and their links, with search.
zweck.tab.parlament: Where laws need majorities: parliamentary groups, talks, alliances and votes.
zweck.tab.verfassung: Changes to the rules of the state: packages, majorities, Constitutional Court and referendum.
zweck.tab.reich_recht: Justice and law: independence, court capacity and compliance with rulings. Reforms cost capital, votes and time, not money.
zweck.tab.waehler: Who backs you and who does not: eleven groups with mood, reasons and demands.
zweck.tab.wahlkampf: The eight weeks before the election: trips across the country, promises with a price, the diaspora, the TV debate, and an opposition that strikes where it hurts.
zweck.tab.wirtschaft: The country's figures and the big levers: central bank and budget.
zweck.tab.reich_haushalt: Budget and administration: administrative strength, building capacity and legitimacy are scarce. Special powers act fast and have a downside.
zweck.tab.reich_infra: What is built needs upkeep; what is being built shares the building capacity. Major projects are wonders with lasting benefits and with opponents.
zweck.tab.reich_kultur: 53 heritage sites decay without care. Wonders, routes and restorations cost capital, construction and administration, hardly any money.
zweck.tab.reich_militaer: The president orders and answers for it, but does not command: programmes run from contract to readiness, doctrines exclude each other.
zweck.tab.katastrophe: When the earth shakes or the water rises: situation, emergency aid and reconstruction.
zweck.tab.welt: The other countries: relations, concerns and negotiations.

lernen.art.massnahme: A measure is a slider you decide on: from level 0 (does not exist) to 100 (as much as possible).
lernen.art.groesse: A quantity describes a state of the country. It changes through your measures, the economy and other quantities.
lernen.art.problem: A problem becomes acute when its value in a province reaches a threshold. It then weighs on trust and the voter groups there.
lernen.art.gruppe: A voter group shows how satisfied part of the population is with your policy. Its mood determines your approval and so the next election.
lernen.begriff.index.name: Index from 0 to 100
lernen.begriff.index.text: To compare very different things, the game expresses many quantities as a number from 0 to 100. It is not a percentage but a scale: higher means more of what the name says. “More” is not always better: more poverty is bad, more jobs are good.
lernen.begriff.durchschnitt.name: National average
lernen.begriff.durchschnitt.text: The mean of the 81 provinces, weighted by population: Istanbul counts more than Tunceli. The average hides differences; the map shows where they are.
lernen.begriff.verzoegerung.name: Delay (“after 3 months”)
lernen.begriff.verzoegerung.text: Policy does not act on the same day. “After 3 months” means the effect arrives three months after the change. That is why the result of a decision often shows only the next year. Dashed arrows in the picture are delayed, solid ones act immediately.
lernen.begriff.akut.name: Acute
lernen.begriff.akut.text: A problem is acute in a province as soon as its value there reaches the threshold. It stays acute until it falls eight points below the threshold, so problems do not flicker on and off.
lernen.begriff.traegheit.name: Inertia
lernen.begriff.traegheit.text: Without a new push, quantities slowly return to their starting value. A short campaign fizzles out, a lasting policy stays.
lernen.begriff.umsetzung.name: Implementation
lernen.begriff.umsetzung.text: A decision is not yet an effect. The slider moves to the new level over several months, and only the implemented share takes effect.
lernen.begriff.realzins.name: Real interest rate
lernen.begriff.realzins.text: The policy rate minus expected inflation. It shows what saving and borrowing really cost: when it is high, saving pays more than spending.
lernen.e.inflation.was1: Inflation measures how much prices have risen compared with the previous year. At 30 per cent, what cost 100 lira a year ago costs 130 lira today.
lernen.e.inflation.was2: You cannot set it. It results from interest rates, demand, people's expectations, energy prices and the lira.
lernen.e.inflation.wichtig: High inflation eats up wages and savings, makes loans expensive and undermines trust. It falls when interest rates stay high, the state does not overspend and people believe the central bank.
lernen.e.inflation.stand: Last published: {wert, number, 1} per cent ({periode}). The central bank's interim target is {ziel, number, 1} per cent; people expect {erwartet, number, 1} per cent.
lernen.e.inflation.stand2: Statistics appear with a delay: you steer by looking in the rear-view mirror.
lernen.e.arbeitslosigkeit.was1: The unemployment rate is the share of the labour force looking for work and not finding it.
lernen.e.arbeitslosigkeit.was2: It follows growth with a delay: only when the economy grows for months are new people hired.
lernen.e.arbeitslosigkeit.wichtig: Unemployment costs income, security and self-confidence. It colours the mood of employees, the young and city dwellers.
lernen.e.arbeitslosigkeit.stand: Last published: {wert, number, 1} per cent ({periode}). In the model it hovers around {lang} per cent in the long run (calibration placeholder).
lernen.e.wachstum.was1: Growth is the change in total economic output (GDP) compared with the previous year.
lernen.e.wachstum.was2: In the policy web it appears as an index: 50 means the economy grows exactly at its potential; above that it overheats, below it stalls.
lernen.e.wachstum.wichtig: Growth creates jobs and tax revenue. Too much growth on credit fuels inflation.
lernen.e.wachstum.stand: Last published: {wert, number, 1} per cent ({periode}). Potential growth in the model is {potenzial, number, 1} per cent.
lernen.e.leitzins.was1: The policy rate is the rate at which banks borrow from the central bank. It affects all loans and the lira.
lernen.e.leitzins.was2: It is set by the central bank's Monetary Policy Committee, not by the president. A president who intervenes risks the markets' trust.
lernen.e.leitzins.wichtig: A high rate curbs demand and inflation and supports the lira, but costs growth and jobs. A low rate does the opposite.
lernen.e.leitzins.stand: Currently {zins, number, 1} per cent; the real rate is {real, number, 1} per cent.
lernen.e.abwertung.was1: Depreciation shows how much more lira one has to pay for a US dollar than twelve months ago (in per cent).
lernen.e.abwertung.was2: If you pay 26 per cent more lira, your lira is only about 21 per cent less valuable against the dollar: a rate that rises by a quarter lowers the value of the other side by a fifth.
lernen.e.abwertung.wichtig: A weak lira makes imports, especially energy, more expensive and drives inflation. Exporters and tourism benefit; anyone with dollar debts loses.
lernen.e.abwertung.stand: Over the last twelve months the dollar costs {x, number, 1} per cent more lira (today {kurs, number, 1} lira). The lira has thus lost about {verlust, number, 1} per cent of its dollar value.
lernen.e.defizit.was1: The budget deficit is the amount by which the state spends more than it takes in, measured as a percentage of economic output.
lernen.e.defizit.was2: In the policy web it appears as an index: 50 means a balanced budget, each point above corresponds to 0.2 percentage points of deficit.
lernen.e.defizit.wichtig: Every deficit becomes debt. Debt costs interest; anyone who owes the markets too much pays with a higher risk premium and a weaker lira.
lernen.e.defizit.stand: The planned deficit is {gesamt, number, 1} per cent of economic output (baseline {grund, number, 1}, your spending programme {programm, number, 1}, cost of your measures {kosten, number, 1}).
lernen.e.schulden.was1: The debt ratio is the state's mountain of debt relative to one year's economic output.
lernen.e.schulden.was2: With high inflation the ratio shrinks by itself, because economic output in lira grows with prices. That is no achievement but a side effect of inflation.
lernen.e.schulden.wichtig: The higher the ratio, the more suspicious the markets and the higher the interest the state has to pay.
lernen.e.schulden.stand: Currently {quote, number, 1} per cent of economic output; the risk premium is {aufschlag, number, 0} basis points.
lernen.m.kostenlos: The measure costs the budget practically nothing.
lernen.m.kostet: At full level it costs about {p, number, 2} per cent of economic output a year compared with level 0. It takes effect only after about {monate, plural, one {# month} other {# months}}.
lernen.m.bringt: At full level it brings in about {p, number, 2} per cent of economic output a year compared with level 0. It takes effect only after about {monate, plural, one {# month} other {# months}}.
lernen.m.stand: It currently stands at level {jetzt} on national average; at the start of your term it was {start}.
lernen.m.beschlossen: Level {ziel} has been decided; implementation is still under way.
lernen.g.stand: The national average is {jetzt, number, 1}; at the start of your term it was {start, number, 1}.
lernen.g.gestiegen: It has risen by {d, number, 1} points.
lernen.g.gesunken: It has fallen by {d, number, 1} points.
lernen.p.keine: The problem is not acute in any province (threshold {schwelle}).
lernen.p.akut: It is acute in {n, plural, one {# province} other {# provinces}} (threshold {schwelle}), most strongly in {orte, list}.
lernen.h.regler: This is itself a slider. What it does is listed under “Effects”; the preview calculates the next twelve months.
lernen.h.keiner: There is no direct slider for this quantity. It follows the causes shown on the left of the picture.

vf.luecke.direkt: The first threshold holds; about {n} votes are expected to be missing for the direct threshold.
vf.luecke.keine: According to the forecast, the direct threshold holds.
vf.absprachenDoppelt: Deals cost double on the constitutional question ({f}×).
vf.angefochten: The opposition has filed a challenge
vf.aym: The Constitutional Court rules in {n, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}. Its make-up ({loyal} loyal, {unabhaengig} independent, {reform} reform-minded) makes annulment look {p, select, selten {unlikely} moeglich {possible} other {likely}}.
vf.referendum: Expected: about {mitte, number, 1} per cent yes (range {tief, number, 1}–{hoch, number, 1}): approval {zustimmung, number, 1}, issues of the articles {salienz}, campaign +{kampagne, number, 1}.
vf.impulsTitel: {pk} capital per push, with a cooldown of one week
vf.werkstattText: One constitutional question per term: bundle a package of up to five articles. Parliament needs {mehrheit} votes (then the people decide) or {direkt} for a direct decision; the Constitutional Court can be called on. Failed articles are blocked for twelve months.
vf.gesperrt: blocked for {n, plural, one {# more day} other {# more days}}
vf.mitVariante: With this option the package would be expected at about {n} yes votes ({delta}).
vf.kosten: Cost: {pk} political capital · expected {n} yes votes (range {tief}–{hoch}).
vf.einbringenTitel: Introduce the package; the vote follows in four weeks
zb.haltung.vorsichtig.name: Strict
zb.haltung.vorsichtig.text: An experienced guardian of price stability: reacts early to inflation and is hard to sway.
zb.haltung.vorsichtig.folge: Markets reward it with some trust; rates stay high, loans expensive.
zb.haltung.ausgewogen.name: Balanced
zb.haltung.ausgewogen.text: An insider: weighs inflation and growth equally, partly yields to pressure.
zb.haltung.ausgewogen.folge: A change remains an intervention; it only partly reassures the markets.
zb.haltung.gefuegig.name: Compliant
zb.haltung.gefuegig.text: Leadership close to the government: prefers cuts, points to growth and jobs and almost always gives in to pressure.
zb.haltung.gefuegig.folge: Markets read it as an attack on independence: the lira falls, the risk premium rises, credibility suffers badly.
zb.druck.zuschlag: Surcharge active (markets are testing the bank)
zb.inTagen: in {n, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}
zb.regel: Without your involvement the bank follows its rule: as things stand it
zb.regel.erhoeht: raises the rate from {alt, number, 1} to {neu, number, 1}%
zb.regel.senkt: cuts the rate from {alt, number, 1} to {neu, number, 1}%
zb.regel.lage: The situation may change by then.
zb.druckLiegt: Pressure is already on for this meeting: {was, select, senkung {you are demanding a cut} other {you are backing the strict line}} ({wie, select, rede {publicly} other {in confidence}}).
zb.weisung: The bank is bound by instructions: you set the rate yourself. Markets see every deviation from the rule ({regel, number, 1}%) and treat it as a political rate.
zb.vorgabeLabel: Policy rate for the next meeting:
zb.bliebe: The rate would stay at {p, number, 1}%. Earlier decisions keep working: what the bank decided in recent months reaches credit, demand and prices only with a delay.
zb.beschliesst: As things stand the bank decides {neu, number, 1}% instead of {regel, number, 1}%.
zb.aendertNichts: As things stand this changes nothing about the decision: the governor sticks to her line.
zb.neubesetzung: Replacing the leadership is a presidential decree: it costs no capital, but market trust. The change is then blocked for {n} days.
zb.geschuetzt: The leadership is protected by law.
zb.wiederIn: Possible again in {n, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}.
zb.gesetzText: Independence changes by law, step by step. It needs the majority of the governing camp (now {lager} of {mehrheit} votes), costs capital, and markets already react to the announcement.
zb.fruehestens: At the earliest in {n, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}.
zb.warnung: Honest warning: net reserves are below {w} billion dollars. Below {d} billion markets demand a surcharge on the exchange rate and risk premium, below {k} billion a balance-of-payments crisis looms.
zb.intervention: Intervention: sell reserves against depreciation pressure
zb.wirkung: Effect: about {g, number, 1}% support for the exchange rate ({s, number, 1}% immediately), net reserves afterwards ${n, number, 1}bn.
zb.verkauftText: The central bank sells {n} billion dollars from its reserves and supports the lira by about {g, number, 1}% over a few weeks.
zb.iwfBruch: The remaining tranches are cancelled. Markets answer the break: risk premium +{n} points, credibility and trust collapse.
zb.iwfAngebot: The IMF puts an offer on the table; decide in the event window.
zb.iwfZoegert: The IMF is hesitating at the moment.

st.umlauf.text: Routine without a decision, collected on your desk.
st.umlauf.badge: Circulation: collected reports without a decision
st.halbjahr.text: Fast-forward stops; the situation remains your business.

st.inflation.tip: Price rise against the same month last year, published by the statistics office with a delay of a few weeks.
st.lira.tip: Market exchange rate, daily. When it rises, imports such as energy become more expensive.
st.leitzins.tip: Set by the central bank's Monetary Policy Committee eight times a year.
